# 1 Clement Chapter 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 28 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_028_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 28

**28:1** Since he sees and hears everything, then, let us fear him and give up the vile desires of evil deeds, so that we may be protected by his mercy from the judgments that are coming.

**28:2** Where can any one of us run from his mighty hand? What world would take in someone who deserts him? As scripture says somewhere:

**28:3** "Where can I go and where can I hide from your face? If I go up to heaven, you are there; if I travel to the ends of the earth, your right hand is there; if I make my bed in the deep, your Spirit is there."

**28:4** So where can anyone escape to, or where can they flee, from the one who holds all things in his embrace?

---

*PNEUMA renders with rhetorical clarity, capturing the urgency of Clement's warning. "Holds all things in his embrace" is more vivid than "encompasses all things" for the final summary.*
